events.summary: Country: World Source: Médecins Sans Frontières Despite generic lenacapavir slowly becoming available for some, Gilead continues to stand in the way of equitable and affordable access amid urgent global need and demand. NEW YORK/JOHANNESBURG, NOVEMBER 26 — In advance of World AIDS Day on December 1, Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is once again calling for more people globally to have access to the highly effective HIV prevention medicine lenacapavir . This twice-yearly injectable version of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is the biggest breakthrough in HIV prevention yet, but US-based Gilead Sciences continues to block affordable access for countries around the world. This includes countries with growing HIV epidemics and ongoing humanitarian crises. As a result of its long-acting nature, lenacapavir may be especially valuable for stigmatized or criminalized populations, who often are excluded from or concerned about accessing health care. It is also a critical tool for people on the move who may struggle to access health clinics, people living in remote areas with few health care options, and people caught in humanitarian emergencies — including those in many of the communities in which MSF operates. “Gilead’s greed alone is the reason people across the globe don’t have access to lenacapavir already,” said Carlota Baptista da Silva, MSF’s global HIV/HCV access and advocacy lead. “Our teams are ready to provide it but have been left empty-handed or with very few doses to offer. In a context emerging from years of largescale conflict, where some conditions have improved but localized violence, new and secondary displacement, and very high humanitarian needs persist in parts of the country, this allocation will fast-track lifesaving and life sustaining multisectoral assistance and protection for crisis affected people in 85 priority subdistricts, which record the highest intersectoral severity of needs and the highest prevalence of IDPs and returnees. The allocation will support the immediate kickstart of the hyper prioritized HNRP, targeting around 4.3 million women, men, girls, boys, older people and persons with disabilities with direct assistance in areas with the highest concentrations of IDPs, returnees and refugees. In this way, the Syria Humanitarian Fund will help translate the humanitarian reset roadmap into concrete action, using pooled funding to drive a principled, highly prioritized and locally empowered response: channeling resources to the most severe needs at speed and scale, minimizing layers and passthrough funding, enabling integrated and multisector programming by best placed actors, and strengthening collective accountability through transparent, evidence based allocation, enhanced monitoring and improved accountability to affected populations. Taken together, the fast‑track reserve, the CERF UFE allocation and the first SHF Standard Allocation form a single, sequenced funding package of over US$200 million designed to save lives in the first half of 2026, while structurally advancing localization through a target of around 75 per cent of SA1 resources to national NGOs and women‑led organizations.

events.summary: Countries: Pakistan, Afghanistan Sources: International Organization for Migration, UN High Commissioner for Refugees Please refer to the attached Infographic. INTRODUCTION In response to the Ministry of Interior's (MoI) decision of 26 September 2023 to enact an “Illegal Foreigners' Repatriation Plan”, UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency and IOM, the UN Migration Agency, have collated their data on the arrest, detention, and deportation of Proof of Registration (PoR) holders, Afghan Citizen Card (ACC) holders, and undocumented Afghan nationals as well as on the outflows of Afghan nationals at the Torkham, Ghulam Khan, Chaman, Badini and Bahramcha border crossing points, to better understand the protection environment and movements of Afghan nationals returning to Afghanistan from Pakistan. n 2025, the Government of Pakistan (GoP) issued several directives impacting Afghan nationals. In January, the GoP announced that Afghan nationals should relocate from Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) and Rawalpindi, or else face deportation. In April, further announcements indicated the implementation of the second phase of the “IFRP”, targeting ACC holders, in addition to undocumented Afghans. In July, the GoP issued a Statutory Regulation Order (SRO) directing the repatriation/deportation of PoR card holders following the expiry of PoR card validity on 30 June. The GoP later indicated a deadline of 1 September for PoR holders to leave Pakistan, before the start of the repatriation/deportation process. UNHCR issued a press briefing expressing concern regarding the decision and urging the GoP to exempt Afghans with international protection needs, as well as those with particular circumstances or vulnerabilities, from involuntary return.

Les personnes déplacées internes, les retournés, les femmes et les enfants demeurent parmi les catégories les plus exposées. Around 862,791 refugees from Ukraine are currently present in Poland, the majority women and children. This represents some 2.5 per cent of the total population of Poland. UNHCR coordinates the response of 58 organizations in Poland under the Ukraine Situation Regional Refugee Response Plan (RRP), the majority of which are local and refugee-led organizations. UNHCR works with the Government of Poland to ensure refugees have access to territory, legal status, documentation and enjoy their rights. HIGHLIGHTS Strengthening access to legal information amid changes to Temporary Protection (TP) Following the entry into force of the Phasing Out Act on 5 March 2026, significant changes were introduced to the temporary protection legal framework in Poland, impacting access to collective accommodation and social assistance with the new eligibility requirements for healthcare coverage. In response, UNHCR scaled up legal information and assistance to help refugees navigate the new framework. Through its eight legal partner organizations, UNHCR provided timely information on changes to temporary protection, including new identity verification requirements for temporary protection holders across Poland. events.summary: Country: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of) Sources: CCCM Cluster, International Organization for Migration, Shelter Cluster, UN High Commissioner for Refugees Please refer to the attached file. 1.Contexto Los terremotos consecutivos de magnitud 7,2 y 7,5 que sacudieron el centro-norte de Venezuela el 24 de junio de 2026 ocasionaron una destrucción generalizada de viviendas, infraestructura pública y servicios esenciales en siete estados: La Guaira, Distrito Capital, Miranda, Aragua, Carabobo, Falcón y Yaracuy. Además de los daños estructurales, la emergencia ha provocado una pérdida generalizada de enseres esenciales para el hogar (EHI), reduciendo la capacidad de las familias para mantener un espacio doméstico funcional. La falta de artículos básicos compromete funciones esenciales de la vida cotidiana, tales como, dormir, cocinar, almacenar agua y comida, acceder a iluminación o electricidad, y realizar prácticas de higiene personal. La ausencia de estos artículos no solo limita la habitabilidad, sino que también afecta la salubridad, protección y la dignidad de las familias. En este escenario, la provisión de kits de enseres esenciales (EHIs) se convierte en un componente clave de la respuesta humanitaria, al garantizar que las personas puedan vivir adecuadamente y con dignidad en sus viviendas, facilitando la recuperación temprana y el retorno seguro a los hogares en las comunidades afectadas.

SHF News Allocations In the second and third quarters of 2026, the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) undertook three critical allocations to address urgent humanitarian needs. In July 2026, the SHF allocated US$ 2 million to scale up response required to mitigate the risk of famine in rural areas of Buurhakaba, Bay Region. The allocation prioritized multisectoral lifesaving assistance to increase access to food, integrated health, nutrition, and protection (GBV) services; and improve access to water. The allocation was complemented by a $10 million CERF Rapid Response grant to sustain humanitarian assistance to mitigate the adverse effects of the prolonged drought conditions in additional areas. In anticipation of a forecast Super El Nino, CERF granted an additional $7 million to facilitate timely, targeted, multi-sectoral interventions in flood high-risk districts along the Juba and Shabelle river basins. Given the gravity of the humanitarian situation amid continuing funding shortfalls, SHF also launched a $21 million Standard Allocation in September to provide integrated multisectoral assistance across seven priority districts hosting underserved communities with the highest severity of needs, including heightened protection and flood risks. Some $13 million from this envelope targeted flood -prone locations. The collective allocation of $33 million from CERF and SHF enabled the strategic use of limited resources through geographic and sectoral convergence, and sectoral complementarity to deliver much needed assistance to vulnerable communities.

Armed violence in Haiti continues to severely disrupt access to health care, forcing numerous health facilities to close, displacing communities, and disrupting medical supply chains. The growing number of internally displaced persons (1.5 million to date) is placing additional pressure on an already overstretched health system. The plant’s connection to its sole remaining external power line, the 330 kV Ferosplavna-1 line, was lost on 25 November at 05:28 local time, reportedly due to military activity. For the 28th time during the conflict, ZNPP is relying on emergency diesel generators for essential nuclear safety and security functions. “Once again we are faced with a loss of offsite power at the ZNPP. events.title: CAR: République Centrafricaine - Initiative Conjointe de Suivi des Marchés (ICSM), octobre - novembre 2026
events.summary: Country: Central African Republic Source: REACH Initiative Please refer to the attached file. MESSAGES CLÉS • Le coût médian du PMAS a diminué sur l’ensemble des marchés évalués avec une baisse de 10% de son prix par rapport à août. Cette tendance a été principalement observée dans la composante alimentaire, tandis que les coûts des paniers de produits non alimentaires et d’hygiène ont connu une hausse. Cependant les marchés de Bangui-Rapide, Boali et Markounda ont connu une hausse importante de leur PMAS. De manière générale, des disparités ont persisté entre les différents marchés, avec un coût médian du PMAS compris entre 40 014 XAF à Bangassou et 102 702 XAF à Dimbi. • La fonctionnalité des marchés est demeurée limitée, avec des scores SFM compris entre 51% et 88%. Cette relative stabilité a masqué des évolutions contrastées entre les différentes dimensions, marquées par une stabilité de la disponibilité des produits, un recul de l’abordabilité et une amélioration des circuits d’approvisionnement. Des améliorations des scores SFM ont été observées à Bangassou, Batangafo et Ngaoundaye, tandis que Bossangoa et Koui ont enregistré une détérioration. L’indisponibilité de certains produits et les difficultés liées à leur abordabilité ont été relevées, parallèlement à des contraintes affectant l’accessibilité des marchés et les circuits d’approvisionnement. Malgré ces évolutions, les écarts de fonctionnalité entre les marchés ont persisté, soulignant des conditions de fonctionnement et d’approvisionnement toujours hétérogènes selon les localités.

events.summary: Countries: World, Malawi Source: Norwegian Refugee Council As the latest El Niño threatens extreme weather across Africa, NORCAP climate experts are turning weather and climate data into early community defences. By Gifty Baah Published 26. Nov 2026 In Malawi, a farmer listening to a seasonal forecast hears that rainfall is likely to be below normal. But one important question remains unanswered: when should I plant? Plant too early and seeds may fail if the rains stop. Plant too late and crops may not reach maturity. For millions of farmers across Africa, these decisions determine whether families harvest enough food, earn an income, or face hardship. This gap between climate information and decision-making, is where NORCAP's work makes a difference. As Africa faces the impacts of the current El Niño event, NORCAP experts embedded in Regional Climate Centres and National Meteorological and Hydrological Services are contributing to transforming climate data into actionable information. Their support is strengthening forecasting systems, building technical capacity, and improving the early warnings that governments, communities and humanitarian agencies rely on to prepare for climate extremes. What is El Niño? A continent facing growing climate risk El Niño is a naturally occurring climate pattern characterised by unusually warm surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. It weakens trade winds and shifts rainfall patterns, influencing weather conditions across the globe. events.title: The Persecution Continues: Minority Communities Under Sustained Attack in Bangladesh (January - October 2026)
events.summary: Country: Bangladesh Source: Human Rights Congress for Bangladesh Minorities Please refer to the attached file. Between 1 January and 31 October 2026, the Human Rights Congress for Bangladesh Minorities (HRCBM) documented 1,445 incidents affecting religious, ethnic, and Indigenous minority communities across all 64 districts and eight administrative divisions of Bangladesh . The Persecution Continues combines national and district-level statistics with representative cases to examine recurring violence, dispossession, and barriers to justice. The documented incidents include 286 reported murders and unexplained deaths , 408 attacks on homes, land, and other property , 251 attacks on temples or other religious sites and incidents of religious vandalism , and 30 blasphemy-related incidents across 14 districts . The report also documents missing-person cases, abductions, physical assaults, and sexual violence. These figures are documented minimums. Fear of retaliation, stigma, and barriers to reporting and verification contribute to underreporting, particularly of sexual violence. The report examines how disputed allegations of religious insult can lead to arrests and retaliation against families and communities, how land grabbing and intimidation can pressure families to leave their homes, and how delays in registering complaints, inadequate investigations, and threats against victims and witnesses can obstruct access to justice. HRCBM calls for equal protection, impartial investigations, effective remedies, and direct participation by affected communities in transitional justice.
